Q: How can i solve this pip wfuzz package instalation error? A:

wfuzz is using a rather old version of pycurl of about 6 years ago.

One way around it :

  1. Install a python virtual environment and activate it.

  2. git clone https://github.com/xmendez/wfuzz.git
    cd wfuzz

  3. remove pycurl from requirements.txt

  4. Run python -m pip install .
    (The final dot is part of the command)

Once you tested fully the virtual environment, then install properly.

Q: How to parse a predictably formatted string and extract multiple values A:

You have a predictably formatted input string which can be directly parsed by PHP's native sscanf(). In most cases, you want to isolate the values wrapped in single-quotes. In the minority of cases, you can either match an expected integer value or match the remainder of the input string. Notice that $entity_id is cast as an int type value. Demo

In my opinion, this is much more professional/clean than exploding and scavenging through the pieces. If sscanf() was not viable, I'd probably parse the input string with preg_match() with "#INF Chat \(from '([^']+)', entity id '(\d+)', to '([^']+)'\): '([^']+)': (.+)#" (Demo). I don't know if any of your values might have spaces in them.

$line = "INF Chat (from 'Steam_76561198379194238', entity id '1298', to 'Global'): 'DavSlo': !test";

sscanf(
    $line,
    "INF Chat (from '%[^']', entity id '%d', to '%[^']'): '%[^']': %s",
    $steam_id,
    $entity_id,
    $chat_audience,
    $player_name,
    $message_text
);

var_export([
    'steam_id' => $steam_id,
    'entity_id' => $entity_id,
    'chat_audience' => $chat_audience,
    'player_name' => $player_name,
    'message_text' => $message_text,
]);

Output:

array (
  'steam_id' => 'Steam_76561198379194238',
  'entity_id' => 1298,
  'chat_audience' => 'Global',
  'player_name' => 'DavSlo',
  'message_text' => '!test',
)

Technically, you could use preg_split() to chop up the string without any post-splitting clean up, but I don't think I'd use this approach professionally. Demo

var_export(
    preg_split("#^[^']+'|'[^']+'|': #", $line, 5, PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY)
);

Q: Java Stream API: Incompatible types: List<ArrayList>> cannot be converted to List<List> A:

The reason for the "incompatible types" error is that the code is attempting to assign a List<ArrayList<String>> to a variable of type List<List<String>>. This is not a valid assignment in Java (for reasons beyond the scope of this answer), hence the error.

The method call Stream.generate(ArrayList<String>::new) is using the specific return type of your supplier function to determine the resulting type of the stream. Since your supplier function returns ArrayList<Stream>, the resulting stream is a Stream<ArrayList<String>>, not a Stream<List<String>>. Calling toList() on this stream (or in your specific case, on the limit(n) stream created from it) results in a List<ArrayList<String>>.

Returning a Stream<List<String>> from Stream.generate

There are a number of ways to have the compiler treat the result of Stream.generate as a Stream<List<String>>, rather than Stream<ArrayList<String>>.

One option (and the one I would personally choose in this case) is to specify explicit type arguments to the Stream.generate method call. This instructs the Java compiler to use the provided type arguments, rather than determining them itself. In your case, you would use List<String> as the type argument to cause a Stream<List<String>> to be returned:

List<List<String>> lists =
        Stream.<List<String>>generate(ArrayList::new).limit(n).toList();

Another option would be to ensure the generator function returns a List<String> as its return type, which results in the compiler using Stream<List<String>> as the type of generate:

List<List<String>> lists = 
        Stream.generate(() -> (List<String>) new ArrayList<String>()).limit(n).toList();

A third option would be to explicitly ensure that the generator function itself is a Supplier<List<String>>, not a Supplier<ArrayList<String>>:

List<List<String>> lists = 
        Stream.generate((Supplier<List<String>>) ArrayList::new).limit(n).toList();
